sentences.text: Researchers analyzed 5.3 million cells from 582 tissue samples collected across 11 brain areas in 55 rhesus macaques ranging from 0.5 to 21 years old to map cellular changes associated with aging.

The analysis revealed specific groups of neurons that disappear with age and slight changes in glial cell composition, alongside molecular patterns resembling those seen in Alzheimer's disease and distinct differences between males and females.
The authors state that this atlas helps understand how different cell types and brain regions are uniquely vulnerable to aging, offering insights that may apply to humans.
